chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadala, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them), that he was asked about the Udhiyah (sacrificial animal), so he said:

"A horned, fat, large-eyed and large-eared male bull is acceptable, and a one-year-old from the sheep is acceptable, and a two-year-old from the goats. And a male sheep is better than a castrated one, and the castrated one is better than a ewe, and the ewe is better than a goat."

And he said: "If he buys a sacrificial animal intending it to be fat, and it turns out to be lean, it is sufficient for him. And if he intends it to be lean and it turns out to be fat, it is sufficient for him. And if he intends it to be lean and it turns out to be lean, it is not sufficient for him."

And he said: "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to sacrifice a horned, large, fat, male ram that ate in blackness and looked in blackness. So if you do not find any of that, then Allah is more deserving of excuse."
And he said: "Females and males from camels and cattle are acceptable."
And I asked him: Is one to sacrifice a castrated animal? He said: "No."

key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةُ: Sacrificial animal offered during Eid al-Adha
key_terms.الْجَذَعُ: A young animal of a specific age (one year old for sheep)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and preferred types of animals for Udhiyah sacrifice in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the juristic criteria for Udhiyah, emphasizing the Prophet’s practice of sacrificing a horned, fat male ram to highlight the virtue of *Iqtir* (pairing) and physical perfection. It clarifies that while intention guides the validity of the sacrifice regarding the animal's condition, castration invalidates it, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the animal's natural integrity. The text also establishes a clear hierarchy of preference among sheep, goats, and cattle, rooted in the Sunnah of the Ahl al-Bayt.
